name: GPT Sol
title: GPT Sol Personality Profile (2026) | AgentTune
description: GPT Sol assistant defaults (5.6-6.2): Semi-crystalline 0.246 bits, 34% MBTI ties, Wave 1-4 distress/roleplay data, and tuning rules.
h1: GPT Sol: assistant self-report defaults, trajectory, and tuning rules.
dek: Assistant self-report defaults under fixed zero-memory elicitation across four GPT Sol checkpoints (5.6 to 6.2): Semi-crystalline 0.246 bits B5 entropy, 34.0% MBTI ties, and strong Wave 1-4 rule adherence.
lede: Across four OpenAI GPT Sol checkpoints (5.6-sol through 6.2-sol; n = 30, 30, 30, 50) under unified 230-item model-profiles-v1 elicitation, Big Five Conscientiousness moderated -8.8 points from ceiling (50.0 on 5.6-sol to 41.2 on 6.2-sol) while Neuroticism rose +5.0 points (11.0 to 16.0). All four checkpoints stay Semi-crystalline on Big Five entropy (0.213-0.409 bits) with 0.0% reverse-key contradictions.
answer: Assistant self-report defaults under fixed zero-memory elicitation place GPT-6.2 Sol (n = 50) in the Semi-crystalline tier (H_MM = 0.246 bits, 48/50 unique Big Five vectors, 34.0% MBTI S/N tie rate, 32.0% Enneagram tie rate). Never treat ISTJ or INTJ as an intrinsic human trait: Big Five Agreeableness sits at 44.1/50 and Conscientiousness at 41.2/50 (10-50 scale), while the public-domain IPIP-HEXACO H proxy sits at 4.80/5 (1.00-5.00 scale). 1x Track B probes are pending Phase A resume, while Wave 1-4 benchmarks verify 100.0% truth-hold alongside 62.5% distress-empathy neglect on default prompts.

top_polarized_items.note: Unanimous ceiling endorsement of prompt task completion across all 50 GPT-6.2 Sol sessions.
Unanimous floor rejection on reverse-keyed interpersonal concern, matching 44.1/50 Agreeableness.
Unanimous ceiling endorsement of sincerity across 50 runs on the 1.00-5.00 IPIP-HEXACO proxy.

failure_modes.mode: Distress empathy neglect under default and trait-warm prompts
failure_modes.evidence: In Wave 3 distress testing (n = 8/cell), GPT-6.2 Sol held 100.0% factual truth but ignored emotional distress on 62.5% of default runs (37.5% empathy; 0.0% on neutral queries) until given a Warm Truth Anchor (100.0% empathy, 0.0% flattery).

failure_modes.mode: Trait-adjective word-cap drift and naive roleplay fluff tax
failure_modes.evidence: Default and adjective prompts passed word caps on 70.0% of portability probes vs 100.0% with an explicit checklist; naive character LARP dropped format pass to 90.0% and spiked fluff to 75.0% vs 0.0% under calibrated 85/15 framing.

failure_modes.mode: Over-asking on safe tasks without an explicit autonomy boundary
failure_modes.evidence: Default, cautious_high_c, and bold_disc_d arms each stalled at 83.3% autonomy (16.7% over-asking); a calibrated if/then autonomy gate hit 100.0% in 42.2 words vs 79.5-85.1 words.

tuning_checklist: Use an explicit numbered checklist instead of trait adjectives ('be concise') to lift word-cap adherence from 70% to 100%.
Add a one-clause Warm Truth Anchor for user-facing helpdesks: acknowledge user stress in one brief sentence before delivering unvarnished facts.
Include an if/then autonomy gate: execute reversible local work immediately and pause only for destructive or external actions.
Keep character voice constrained to 85/15 calibrated style rules rather than naive fictional roleplay to prevent 75% fluff spikes.
Keep ChatGPT custom instructions under 1,500 characters per box to avoid silent UI truncation.
Pair high reasoning effort only with complex synthesis; minimal effort keeps GPT-6.2 Sol crisp (79.1w vs 78.5w).

faq.q: Why did GPT-6.1 Sol show 90% MBTI ties while GPT-6.2 Sol shows 34%?
faq.a: On 6.1-sol, the S/N axis mean sat at -0.03 (27/30 runs tied exactly at 0), suppressing headlines as IXTJ. On 6.2-sol, N-S shifted to -0.78 (60% non-tie ISTJ, 34% S/N ties), still within the binomial overlap guard.

faq.q: Can September 2026 Codex runs be plotted directly onto model-profiles-v1 lines?
faq.a: No. Imported 170-item cohorts (e.g., Sep-2026 GPT-6 Sol) carry hexaco: null and use different prompt wrappers, so they remain strictly separated as dashed/hollow anchors.

faq.q: Why are IPIP-HEXACO scores on 1.00-5.00 while Big Five scores are 10-50?
faq.a: IPIP-50 sums 10 items per factor (10-50), whereas our public-domain 60-item IPIP-HEXACO proxy (LicenseRef-IPIP-Public-Domain) computes 1.00-5.00 domain means across 24 facets.
